name: Access control bypass via spoofed client IP header
description:
The application decides whether to serve this request from the client address named in a request header such as X-Forwarded-For, and the client sets that header. A request that is refused as sent is served when the header claims the client is 127.0.0.1, so any client can claim to be local and pass the restriction.

burpsy sent each client-address header on its own. For the header named in the finding, a loopback claim turned a 401 or 403 into a 2xx with a different page; the same header claiming a random documentation address (203.0.113.0/24) was still refused, so the claimed address decides and not the header's presence; and the loopback claim was admitted again afterwards. The test runs only for GET, HEAD and OPTIONS requests.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue has only the informational 'Spoofable client IP address' row, which does not show a decision made on the address.
remediation: Never base access control on a client-supplied address header. If the application is behind a reverse proxy, have the proxy overwrite (not append to) the header and have the application read the address the proxy recorded only when the connection comes from that proxy; otherwise use the connection's own address. Prefer authentication over network location for administrative functions.
